<explanation>
Based on the files and README provided, here’s how you can create a clear, detailed system design diagram tailored to this project:

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose:
   • This repository isn’t a full-stack web application; instead, it’s an archival/configuration repository focused on storing and organizing system prompts and AI model definitions. It “houses” several types of textual configuration files associated with two major AI agent systems—one identified by “v0” (including its models and tools) and another for “Cursor” (with its agent file and pending additions)—along with a dedicated folder for Manus Agent Tools and Prompt.
   • The README confirms the collection of over 5k lines of official system prompts and models, indicating its focus on configuring “agent” behavior for AI tools.

2. Analyze the File Structure:
   • Top-Level Files: Files such as DISCLAIMER.md, v0.txt, v0 model.txt, v0 tools.txt, and cursor agent.txt indicate core artifacts representing different system configurations.
   • Dedicated Directory “Manus Agent Tools & Prompt”: This directory further structures parts of the Manus system. It contains:
       - "agent loop": which likely defines the main iterative or control logic for the agent.
       - "modules": which suggests extensibility via modular components.
       - "prompt.txt" and "tools.json": configuration files specific to the Manus agent tools.
   • The structure shows a separation between different AI system configurations (v0, Cursor, and Manus), which hints at an architectural separation of concerns.

3. Determine the Main Components:
   • v0 Components: 
       - v0.txt – primary system prompt or configuration.
       - v0 model.txt – definitions or parameters for the AI model.
       - v0 tools.txt – tool configurations that interface with the v0 model.
   • Cursor Components:
       - cursor agent.txt – agent definition for the Cursor system.
       - (Future files such as cursor ask.txt and cursor edit.txt are mentioned, emphasizing ongoing development.)
   • Manus Components:
       - “Manus Agent Tools & Prompt” folder is a module that contains its own “agent loop”, “modules”, and configuration files (prompt.txt and tools.json). This group likely forms the backbone of the Manus agent’s operational logic.
   • Documentation:
       - README.md and DISCLAIMER.md serve as meta-documents that provide user guidance and legal information.

4. Relationships and Interactions:
   • Although the repository mainly consists of configuration and prompt files, it is useful to show how each set of files contributes to an overall “agent-based” system.
   • Think of the diagram as comprising several blocks:
       - A block representing the v0 AI system configured by its trio of files. An arrow can indicate that v0.txt feeds into both the v0 model and v0 tools components.
       - A block for the Cursor agent where the "cursor agent.txt" sets the initial configuration or behavior, with future expansions anticipated.
       - A block for the Manus agent tools, which is modular. Within this block, show a “agent loop” sub-component that drives the agent’s execution cycle, a “modules” sub-component that extends functionality, and configuration files (prompt.txt and tools.json) that define operational parameters.
   • Use directional arrows to represent data or configuration flow between these components. For instance, you may illustrate how the Manus configuration (from prompt.txt and tools.json) feeds into the agent loop, which in turn may interact with various modules.

5. Architectural Patterns and Technologies:
   • Although not a conventional service-based system, the repository uses a modular design pattern. Each agent system (v0, Cursor, Manus) is self-contained but conceptually part of a larger AI tool ecosystem.
   • No specific frameworks are mentioned, so assume the use of plain text configuration and possibly scripting to drive the agent behaviour.
   • Emphasize design principles such as separation of concerns (each system is kept in distinct files or directories), modularity (the Manus folder shows a modular design), and clarity in configuration.

6. Guidelines for Drawing the Diagram:
   • Clearly label each major component:
       - “v0 AI Configuration”: with sub-components labeled v0.txt, v0 model.txt, and v0 tools.txt.
       - “Cursor AI Agent”: label the component (cursor agent.txt, plus any future files).
       - “Manus Agent Tools”: with sub-components for “Agent Loop”, “Modules”, and configuration files (prompt.txt & tools.json).
       - “Documentation”: for README and DISCLAIMER files (as a supportive block).
   • Use directional arrows to show how configuration files “feed” into the functioning of each agent system. For example, arrows from v0.txt to both the model.txt and tools.txt components, reflecting data or control flow.
   • Differentiate component types visually:
       - Use different shapes or colors (e.g., rectangles for main modules, sub-rectangles for configuration files) to clearly separate functional areas.
       - Consider color coding: one color for v0 components, another for Cursor, and a third for Manus.
   • Position the components in a layout that reflects their role:
       - Perhaps a left-to-right or top-to-bottom flow showing initial configuration inputs (the text prompt files) leading into “processing” components (agent loops and modules) and then to outputs (which may be the integrated AI behavior).

7. Additional Tips for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • For this type of archival/configuration repository, the diagram should focus on illustrating the clear separation and interaction between distinct prompt/model groups rather than server-client interactions.
   • Focus on capturing every file group as a “node” on the diagram without overcomplicating inter-dependencies—this makes the overall architecture transparent.
   • Include annotations or brief descriptions for each component explaining their role (for example, "v0 model.txt: Defines model parameters for the v0 AI agent").
   • Finally, emphasize that while the repository itself is static, the diagram is designed to help understand how these static components would be integrated into an operational AI system.

Following these steps, your system design diagram will accurately and clearly represent the architecture of this project and provide a valuable reference for understanding the modular configuration of its various AI agent systems.
</explanation>
